description: We are a team of explorers and innovators who connect technology, science, and data to transform the way we understand our planet.
summary:
Groundy is a decision-support system that translates NASA Earth observation data (POWER, SMAP, MODIS, and GPM IMERG) into practical agronomic recommendations. Unlike other platforms, Groundy makes the true scale of information visible, mapping the actual footprint of climate data directly over the farmer's plot so they can understand their context. Using this foundation, the system evaluates the suitability of 42 crops and designs resilient rotations. Furthermore, farmers can log their plantings, activities, and harvests, building a verifiable history secured by cryptographic hashes.

To bridge the rural connectivity gap, the Groundy engine runs locally on a small single-board computer (Orange Pi 5B). It acts as an autonomous on-farm server that synchronizes and stores processed data from Google Earth Engine and NASA POWER, along with the farmer's records, when connectivity is available through our API. Thus, in areas without Internet, both analyses and historical records remain accessible, ensuring scalability to IoT solutions without relying on the network.

Finally, Papanauta, our AI assistant, explains these results by combining farm data with agronomic knowledge, ensuring the technology is understandable and useful.
details:
What it does and how it works
Groundy transforms complex satellite data into simple agricultural decisions. The farmer draws their plot using MapLibre and Terra Draw, and the data is saved locally in their browser with IndexedDB and Dexie. When analyzing the plot, the FastAPI backend queries Google Earth Engine and NASA POWER to calculate the suitability of 42 crops and suggest rotations. All this information is displayed in a clean interface where the farmer can interact with Potatonaut, our AI assistant, to understand the results in simple language.

Benefits and Intended Impact
The main impact is the democratization of science. Groundy does not hide uncertainty; it maps the actual footprint of the data so the farmer knows how accurate the information is for their plot. Furthermore, it aims to revitalize the agricultural sector, which faces significant aging and low youth participation. By running the engine on an Orange Pi 5B, we enable the tool to work in rural areas without internet, betting on a tech-driven agriculture that is attractive to new generations.

Tools and Technologies Used
Frontend developed with React, Vite, and TypeScript, hosted on GitHub Pages. For the backend, we use Python and FastAPI, deployed on an Orange Pi 5B behind a Cloudflare tunnel. For satellite data, we integrate Google Earth Engine and NASA POWER. Local database uses IndexedDB with Dexie, and caching is managed via Supabase. The conversational AI uses the Gemini API with RAG techniques.

Creativity and Factors Considered
Our creativity lies in bringing the cloud down to the ground, packaging the system into accessible hardware to eliminate internet dependency. We also created a character (Potatonaut) to make the AI friendly and less intimidating. We considered critical factors such as intermittent connectivity, the spatial resolution of data, and the need for the system to be scalable to integrate IoT sensors in the future.
